description: The computer cannot reach the internet at all. This may show as 'No Internet' next to the network icon, and no websites or online apps work.
symptoms: Network icon shows a red X or 'No Internet' warning
Browser shows 'This site can't be reached' for all websites
No apps that need internet will load or sync
possible_causes: Modem or router is powered off or malfunctioning
ISP outage in the area
Cable (Ethernet) unplugged or WiFi disconnected
Wrong network settings (IP, DNS, gateway)
Network adapter driver problem
Firewall or antivirus blocking all traffic
diagnostic_questions: Is only this computer affected, or all devices on the network?
Are the modem and router powered on with normal-looking lights?
Is this a wired or wireless connection?
Did this start suddenly or after any recent change, like a storm, move, or software install?

commands.purpose: Check the computer's current IP address, gateway, and DNS settings
commands.expected_result: Valid IP address, subnet, gateway, and DNS shown for the active adapter
commands.abnormal_result: No IP address, or an address starting with 169.254.x.x, meaning no valid network config was received

commands.purpose: Test raw internet connectivity to a known reliable IP address, bypassing DNS
commands.expected_result: Replies received
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning there is no path to the internet at all

commands.purpose: Test internet connectivity including DNS name resolution
commands.expected_result: Replies received with google.com resolved to an IP
commands.abnormal_result: 'Ping request could not find host' means a DNS problem rather than a raw connectivity problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if other devices on the same network (phone, another computer) also have no internet
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Determines if the problem is with this computer specifically or the whole network/ISP

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the modem and router for normal status lights, especially the internet/WAN light
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An abnormal or off WAN light usually points to an ISP-side or modem problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run ipconfig /all to check if the computer has a valid IP address
troubleshooting_steps.reason: No valid IP means the computer never properly joined the local network

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping 8.8.8.8 to test raw connectivity, then ping google.com to test DNS
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Separates a pure connectivity problem from a DNS-only problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the modem and router by powering them off for 30 seconds, then back on
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves the majority of temporary ISP and router connection issues

troubleshooting_steps.action: Contact the ISP if the WAN light stays off or red after a restart
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Indicates an outage or line problem outside the local network

possible_solutions: Restart modem and router
Check and reseat all cables
Renew the IP address with ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew
Contact ISP if the outage is confirmed on their end
Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
prevention: Use a surge protector for modem and router
Keep router firmware updated
Avoid unplugging networking equipment during active updates

description: The network icon shows a normal connected status, but web pages will not load in the browser.
symptoms: Network status shows connected with no warning icon
Browser shows 'This site can't be reached' or keeps loading forever
Other network apps like games or file sync may still work
possible_causes: DNS server not resolving website names
Browser-specific issue like cache, extensions, or proxy settings
Firewall blocking the browser specifically
ISP DNS server down
Malware redirecting or blocking browser traffic
diagnostic_questions: Does this happen in all browsers or just one?
Can you browse using a mobile data connection to compare?
Have you tried visiting a website by typing its raw IP address?
Were any new browser extensions or antivirus programs installed recently?

commands.purpose: Check if raw internet connectivity works even though browsing fails
commands.expected_result: Replies received, confirming the internet connection itself is fine
commands.abnormal_result: Timeout would mean this is not just a browser issue but a deeper connectivity problem

commands.purpose: Test whether DNS name resolution is working
commands.expected_result: Returns an IP address for google.com
commands.abnormal_result: 'DNS request timed out' or no answer means DNS resolution is failing

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping 8.8.8.8 to confirm the raw internet connection works
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If this succeeds, the problem is isolated to DNS or the browser, not the network connection itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run nslookup on a well-known domain to test DNS resolution
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether DNS is the specific point of failure

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different browser to see if the problem is browser-specific
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Narrows the cause to one application versus the whole system

troubleshooting_steps.action: Change the DNS server to a public one like 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1 in network adapter settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Bypasses a malfunctioning ISP DNS server

troubleshooting_steps.action: Clear the browser cache and disable extensions one by one
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Corrupted cache or a bad extension can block or break page loading

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a malware scan if the problem persists across all browsers and DNS changes
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some malware intercepts or redirects browser traffic silently

possible_solutions: Change DNS server to a public DNS like 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1
Clear browser cache and cookies
Disable browser extensions one at a time to find the culprit
Run a malware/antivirus scan
Reset the browser to default settings
prevention: Keep browser and extensions updated
Avoid installing browser extensions from unknown sources
Periodically clear browser cache

description: Windows shows 'Limited' next to the network connection, meaning the device is connected to the local network but cannot reach the internet properly.
symptoms: Network icon shows a yellow warning triangle or 'Limited' status
Local network devices may be reachable, but internet is not
Sometimes intermittently works then drops back to limited
possible_causes: Router failed to provide internet access even though local connection is fine
APIPA address (169.254.x.x) assigned instead of a real DHCP address
Router's WAN connection to the ISP is down
Network adapter driver issue
diagnostic_questions: Does the IP address shown start with 169.254?
Is the router's internet/WAN light on and normal?
Can you access other devices on the local network, like a printer or another computer?
Does restarting the adapter or router fix it temporarily?

commands.purpose: Check the current IP address type and range
commands.expected_result: A normal private IP like 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x
commands.abnormal_result: An address starting with 169.254.x.x (APIPA) confirms no valid DHCP address was received

commands.purpose: Release the current IP address configuration
commands.expected_result: Adapter releases its IP with no error
commands.abnormal_result: Error releasing may indicate a deeper adapter or driver issue

commands.purpose: Request a new IP address from the DHCP server
commands.expected_result: A valid new IP address is assigned
commands.abnormal_result: Renewal fails or still returns a 169.254.x.x address, pointing to a DHCP or router problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the IP address with ipconfig to see if it is an APIPA (169.254.x.x) address
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms the computer failed to get an address from the router's DHCP service

troubleshooting_steps.action: Release and renew the IP address using ipconfig /release then ipconfig /renew
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Forces a fresh request for network configuration

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router if renewal fails or the same APIPA address returns
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The router's DHCP service may have stopped or crashed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router's WAN status to confirm it has internet from the ISP
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A router without WAN internet can still hand out local IPs but with limited access

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the network adapter driver if the problem is isolated to one computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An outdated or corrupted driver can prevent proper DHCP negotiation

possible_solutions: Release and renew the IP address
Restart the router
Update the network adapter driver
Manually set a static IP as a temporary workaround
Check ISP status if the router's WAN connection is down
prevention: Keep router firmware updated
Ensure the router's DHCP pool is large enough for all connected devices
Restart the router periodically if it is older hardware

description: The internet connection works but is much slower than expected, with pages loading slowly and downloads taking longer than normal.
symptoms: Web pages load slowly
Streaming buffers frequently
Download and upload speeds are far below the subscribed plan
Speed test results are consistently low
possible_causes: Too many devices using bandwidth at the same time
Weak WiFi signal instead of wired connection
ISP throttling or an outage affecting speed
Malware or background applications using bandwidth
Outdated router hardware or firmware
Physical line or cable issues
diagnostic_questions: Is this slow on all devices or just one?
Are you connected by WiFi or Ethernet cable?
How many devices are actively using the internet right now?
Have you run a speed test, and how does it compare to your subscribed plan?

commands.purpose: Check for high latency or inconsistent response times that could explain slowness
commands.expected_result: Consistent low response times, for example under 50ms
commands.abnormal_result: High or wildly varying response times suggest network congestion or an unstable connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a speed test connected via Ethernet cable directly to the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out WiFi signal issues and tests the true line speed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check how many devices are connected and actively using bandwidth, such as downloads or streaming
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Bandwidth is shared, and heavy usage by other devices reduces available speed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the modem and router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears temporary congestion or performance issues in the networking equipment

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for background applications or updates consuming bandwidth on the affected computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Automatic updates or cloud sync tools can silently use large amounts of bandwidth

troubleshooting_steps.action: Compare the speed test result to the plan speed from the ISP
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether this is a real problem or expected performance for the plan

troubleshooting_steps.action: Contact the ISP if wired speeds are consistently far below the subscribed plan
troubleshooting_steps.reason: May indicate a line problem or an area-wide issue on their end

possible_solutions: Connect via Ethernet cable to rule out WiFi issues
Limit the number of simultaneous heavy-bandwidth devices
Restart modem and router
Close bandwidth-heavy background applications
Contact ISP if wired speed remains consistently low
prevention: Regularly restart networking equipment
Keep router firmware updated for best performance
Position the router centrally to improve WiFi speed for all devices

description: The internet connection drops and reconnects repeatedly throughout the day instead of staying stable.
symptoms: Internet works, then disconnects briefly, then reconnects on its own
Video calls or streaming cut out periodically
Network icon flickers between connected and disconnected
possible_causes: Loose or damaged Ethernet cable or connector
WiFi interference from other devices or networks
Overheating router or modem
ISP-side intermittent line issue
Outdated network driver causing periodic disconnects
IP address conflict causing intermittent drops
diagnostic_questions: Does the disconnect happen at regular intervals or randomly?
Is this on WiFi or a wired connection?
Does the router or modem feel warm or hot to the touch?
Does the problem happen on all devices at the same time, suggesting a router/ISP issue, or just one device?

commands.purpose: Continuously ping to observe exactly when and how often the connection drops
commands.expected_result: Continuous replies with no gaps
commands.abnormal_result: Periodic timeouts corresponding to when the user notices disconnects, confirming an unstable connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a continuous ping test while using the computer normally to capture the exact drop pattern
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides objective evidence of when and how often the connection actually drops

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check and reseat all physical cable connections, or try a different cable
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A loose or damaged cable is a very common cause of intermittent drops

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the router or modem feels excessively warm and ensure it has proper ventilation
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Overheating equipment can intermittently reset or drop connections

troubleshooting_steps.action: Move the router away from interference sources like microwaves, cordless phones, or thick walls if using WiFi
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Interference is a common cause of periodic WiFi drops

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the network adapter driver on the affected computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Outdated drivers can cause periodic reconnections due to power-saving or compatibility bugs

troubleshooting_steps.action: Contact the ISP to check the line if the issue affects all devices and persists after equipment checks
troubleshooting_steps.reason: May indicate an external line quality issue

possible_solutions: Replace damaged or loose cables
Improve router ventilation and placement
Reduce WiFi interference sources
Update network adapter drivers
Contact ISP to check line quality if the problem is network-wide
prevention: Use quality cables and connectors
Keep networking equipment in a cool, ventilated location
Regularly update router firmware and device drivers

description: The internet connection disconnects completely and requires manual reconnection or a router restart multiple times per day.
symptoms: Connection drops fully and does not reconnect automatically
Manual reconnect or router restart is needed each time
Happens multiple times daily, more severe than brief intermittent drops
possible_causes: Router firmware bug or crash
ISP modem/router experiencing hardware failure
Overloaded router from too many connected devices
IP address lease conflicts
Power supply issues to the router or modem
diagnostic_questions: How many times per day does this happen, roughly?
Does restarting the router fix it every time, or does it sometimes need longer to recover?
How old is the router/modem, and has firmware ever been updated?
How many devices are typically connected to this network?

commands.purpose: Check for a valid IP address after a disconnect to see how the computer's network state looks
commands.expected_result: A valid, current IP address and gateway
commands.abnormal_result: Missing or APIPA address suggests the router itself dropped and did not properly hand out addresses

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router's firmware version and update to the latest available version
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Many frequent-disconnect issues are fixed by manufacturers in firmware updates

troubleshooting_steps.action: Count and review all connected devices for one that might be overloading the router, such as a device downloading heavily
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An overloaded router can crash or drop connections under heavy load

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the power supply and cable to the router/modem for looseness or damage
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Power interruptions can cause the equipment to reset unexpectedly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Perform a factory reset on the router if firmware updates do not help
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears any corrupted configuration causing instability

troubleshooting_steps.action: Replace the router if it is old and resets continue after a factory reset and firmware update
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Aging hardware often becomes unstable over time

possible_solutions: Update router firmware
Reduce the number of connected devices or upgrade to router hardware that supports more devices
Check and secure the power connection to the router
Factory reset the router if problems continue
Replace aging router hardware
prevention: Keep firmware updated on a regular schedule
Avoid overloading a single router with excessive devices
Use a UPS to protect against power fluctuations

description: Network responses take longer than normal, causing lag in video calls, online games, or any real-time application, even though the connection is otherwise working.
symptoms: Video calls have noticeable delay or lag
Online games show high ping numbers
Ping tests return high response times, for example over 100-150ms for a normally low-latency connection
possible_causes: Network congestion from other devices
WiFi instead of wired connection adding latency
ISP routing issue or distant server location
Router processing overload
Background applications consuming bandwidth
diagnostic_questions: What ping time are you seeing, and what would you normally expect?
Is this happening on WiFi or a wired connection?
Does the high latency happen with everything, or only specific applications or servers?
Are other devices on the network actively using a lot of bandwidth right now?

commands.purpose: Measure average latency over multiple pings to a general destination
commands.expected_result: Consistent, low response times appropriate for the connection type
commands.abnormal_result: Consistently high or highly variable response times confirm a latency problem

commands.purpose: Identify at which hop along the route latency increases significantly
commands.expected_result: Latency increases gradually and reasonably at each hop
commands.abnormal_result: A large latency jump at a specific hop points to where the delay is being introduced, such as the ISP or a specific server

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a ping test to a well-known server to measure current latency
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Establishes a baseline number to work with

troubleshooting_steps.action: Switch from WiFi to a wired Ethernet connection if possible and re-test
troubleshooting_steps.reason: WiFi commonly adds extra latency compared to a wired connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for other devices or applications using heavy bandwidth at the same time
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Congestion from other traffic increases queuing delay

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run tracert to see where along the path latency increases sharply
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Helps determine if the delay is local, at the ISP, or further along the internet route

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router to clear any processing overload
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves temporary router performance issues contributing to latency

troubleshooting_steps.action: Contact the ISP if tracert shows the delay starting outside the local network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The issue may be in their network or peering routes, outside local control

possible_solutions: Switch to a wired connection to reduce latency
Reduce simultaneous bandwidth usage from other devices
Restart the router
Contact the ISP if the delay is confirmed to originate outside the local network
prevention: Use wired connections for latency-sensitive activities like gaming or video calls
Avoid heavy downloads during important real-time sessions
Choose servers geographically closer when possible for online applications

description: Some data packets sent over the network never arrive at their destination, causing choppy calls, game rubber-banding, or incomplete data transfers.
symptoms: Video or voice calls sound choppy or cut out briefly
Online games show rubber-banding or missed hits
Ping tests show some requests timing out while others succeed
possible_causes: Weak or interfered WiFi signal
Damaged network cable or faulty port
Network congestion overloading equipment
Faulty router, switch, or modem hardware
ISP-side network issue
diagnostic_questions: Is this happening on WiFi or a wired connection?
What percentage of packet loss are you seeing in a ping test?
Does packet loss happen constantly or only at certain times of day?
Have you tried testing from a different device or location to compare?

commands.purpose: Send many pings to calculate a percentage of lost packets
commands.expected_result: 0% packet loss, or very close to it
commands.abnormal_result: Noticeable packet loss percentage (for example, above 1-2%) confirms a real problem

commands.purpose: Identify which hop in the network path is dropping packets
commands.expected_result: All hops respond consistently
commands.abnormal_result: A specific hop showing repeated timeouts or high loss indicates where the problem is occurring

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run an extended ping test and check the packet loss percentage in the summary
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Quantifies the severity of the problem with concrete numbers

troubleshooting_steps.action: Switch to a wired connection if currently on WiFi and re-test
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Wireless interference is a very common cause of packet loss

troubleshooting_steps.action: Inspect and replace network cables between the computer, switch, and router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A damaged cable can cause consistent packet loss

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run tracert to identify which specific hop is dropping packets
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Helps determine if the loss is local, at the router, or somewhere in the ISP's network

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart networking equipment (router, switch, modem) to rule out a temporary hardware glitch
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears buffer overflows or temporary faults causing packet drops

troubleshooting_steps.action: Contact the ISP if packet loss is confirmed beyond the local network in the tracert results
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The issue lies outside what can be fixed locally

possible_solutions: Switch from WiFi to a wired connection
Replace damaged network cables
Restart routers, switches, and modems
Contact the ISP if loss is confirmed on their network segment
prevention: Use quality, undamaged cables
Position WiFi routers to minimize interference and obstruction
Monitor network equipment for early signs of hardware failure

description: The internet works normally for most sites, but one or a few specific websites will not load, while everything else works fine.
symptoms: Most websites load normally
One or a few specific sites time out, show an error, or never load
Other devices may or may not have the same problem with those sites
possible_causes: The specific website itself is down or having issues
DNS cache holding outdated or incorrect information for that site
ISP or regional block/throttling of that specific site
Firewall or security software blocking that particular domain
Browser-specific cache or cookie issue for that site
diagnostic_questions: Which specific website or websites are affected?
Does the site fail on all your devices, or just this one?
Have you tried accessing the site from a different network, like mobile data?
Have you tried clearing your browser cache or using a private/incognito window for that site?

commands.purpose: Check basic reachability to the specific website's server
commands.expected_result: Replies received (though some sites block ping deliberately)
commands.abnormal_result: Timeout may indicate a routing or blocking issue, though it is not conclusive since many sites disable ping responses

commands.purpose: Confirm the domain resolves to a valid IP address
commands.expected_result: Returns a valid IP address for the domain
commands.abnormal_result: No response or an unexpected IP may indicate a DNS caching or resolution problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the website is down for everyone using a third-party outage checking site or by testing from another network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a problem on your end if the site itself is having issues

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try opening the site in a private/incognito browser window
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Bypasses cached cookies and data that might be causing the specific site to fail

troubleshooting_steps.action: Flush the DNS cache using ipconfig /flushdns
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears any outdated or corrupted cached DNS entry for that specific domain

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try accessing the site using a different DNS server, such as 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some ISP DNS servers have issues resolving specific domains correctly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check firewall or security software logs for the domain being specifically blocked
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Security software or parental controls sometimes block specific sites intentionally

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the site from mobile data to determine if the block is specific to this network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether the restriction is local (ISP/router/firewall) or on the site's end

possible_solutions: Flush the DNS cache
Try a different public DNS server
Clear browser cache/cookies or use a private window
Check and adjust firewall or security software rules for that domain
Wait if the site itself is confirmed down
prevention: Keep a note of frequently used sites' normal behavior to quickly spot anomalies
Keep DNS and security software configurations well documented
Regularly clear browser cache to avoid stale site data

problem: Internet Works on Other Devices Only
description: Every device on the network has internet access except one specific computer, which shows no connection or limited access.
symptoms: Phones, tablets, and other computers connect fine
One specific computer has no internet or limited access
Problem persists even after restarting the router
possible_causes: Network adapter driver issue on the affected computer
IP address conflict specific to that device
Incorrect network settings (static IP, DNS, proxy) on that computer only
Firewall or security software on that computer blocking traffic
Faulty network adapter hardware or cable specific to that device
diagnostic_questions: Is this a wired or wireless connection on the affected computer?
Have any network settings been manually changed on this computer, like a static IP or proxy?
Does the problem happen only on this network, or also elsewhere?
Was any new security software or VPN installed recently on this computer?

commands.purpose: Check the affected computer's specific network configuration for problems
commands.expected_result: Valid IP, subnet, gateway, and DNS matching the rest of the network
commands.abnormal_result: APIPA address, wrong subnet, incorrect static IP, or missing gateway explains why only this device fails

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run ipconfig /all on the affected computer and compare its settings to a working device on the same network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Quickly reveals if the configuration is different or invalid on the problem computer

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for a manually configured static IP, DNS, or proxy setting that may be incorrect
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Manual settings are a common cause of a single device failing while others work fine

troubleshooting_steps.action: Set the network adapter back to automatic (DHCP) IP and DNS settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Removes any incorrect manual configuration as the cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Temporarily disable firewall or security software to test if it is blocking the connection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Overly aggressive security software can block all internet traffic on just one machine

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different network cable or, for WiFi, try a different WiFi adapter if available, to test for a hardware fault
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Isolates whether the issue is a failing physical network component

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A corrupted or outdated driver can cause connectivity to fail on just this device

possible_solutions: Reset network adapter settings to automatic (DHCP)
Disable conflicting security software temporarily to test
Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
Replace a faulty cable or adapter
prevention: Avoid manually changing network settings unless necessary and well documented
Keep network drivers updated
Review security software rules after installation to ensure they don't block normal traffic
keywords: other devices work fine but not this one

description: Windows or the network status shows the Ethernet cable as unplugged, even though a cable appears to be connected.
symptoms: Notification or icon says 'Network cable unplugged'
No network connection through the wired port
Cable appears physically connected
possible_causes: Cable not fully seated in the port
Damaged cable or connector
Faulty Ethernet port on the computer or router/switch
Cable plugged into the wrong port
Network adapter disabled
diagnostic_questions: Have you tried unplugging and firmly replugging the cable at both ends?
Have you tried a different, known-working cable?
Does the port's link light turn on when the cable is plugged in?
Have you tried plugging the cable into a different port on the router or switch?

commands.purpose: Check the Ethernet adapter's current status
commands.expected_result: Adapter shows 'Media State: Media disconnected' only if truly unplugged; otherwise a valid IP appears
commands.abnormal_result: Persistent 'Media disconnected' despite a plugged-in cable confirms a physical link problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Unplug the Ethernet cable and firmly reinsert it at both the computer and router/switch ends until it clicks
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A cable not fully seated is the most common and simplest cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the small link/activity light near the Ethernet port lights up when connected
troubleshooting_steps.reason: No light at all usually confirms a physical connection or port problem rather than a software issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different, known-working Ethernet cable
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a damaged cable as the cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try plugging into a different port on the router or switch
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Isolates whether the router/switch port itself has failed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Device Manager to confirm the network adapter is enabled and not disabled or missing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A disabled adapter can sometimes show a similar 'unplugged' style message

possible_solutions: Firmly reseat the cable at both ends
Replace a damaged Ethernet cable
Use a different port on the router or switch
Enable the network adapter if it was disabled
prevention: Use good quality cables and avoid excessive bending or pulling
Label and route cables neatly to avoid accidental disconnection
Periodically inspect cable connectors for wear

description: The Ethernet connection shows as 'Not connected' in network settings, with no active link to the router or switch.
symptoms: Ethernet adapter listed but shows 'Not connected' status
No internet or local network access via the wired connection
May happen consistently or only sometimes
possible_causes: Cable, port, or adapter hardware fault
Adapter disabled in Windows or Device Manager
Driver issue preventing the adapter from establishing a link
Switch or router port not active or misconfigured
Duplex/speed mismatch between adapter and switch
diagnostic_questions: Does the port's link light turn on with the cable connected?
Is the network adapter enabled in Device Manager and network settings?
Has this connection worked before on this exact cable and port?
Have any recent driver or Windows updates been installed?

commands.purpose: View detailed adapter state including media connection status
commands.expected_result: Shows a connected state with a valid IP address
commands.abnormal_result: Shows 'Media disconnected' or the adapter missing entirely

commands.purpose: View the status of all network adapters from PowerShell
commands.expected_result: Ethernet adapter status shows 'Up'
commands.abnormal_result: Status shows 'Disabled', 'Disconnected', or the adapter is missing from the list

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the cable is properly connected and check for a link light on both ends
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a basic physical connection issue first

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Device Manager to ensure the Ethernet adapter is enabled and has no warning icons
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A disabled or malfunctioning adapter will never show as connected

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run Get-NetAdapter in PowerShell to check the adapter's detailed status
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Gives clear technical confirmation of whether the adapter itself is up or down

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update or reinstall the Ethernet adapter driver
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A corrupted or incompatible driver can prevent the adapter from establishing a link

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the same cable and port with another device if possible
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether the fault is with this specific computer or the network side

possible_solutions: Reseat or replace the cable
Enable the adapter in Device Manager if disabled
Update or reinstall the Ethernet driver
Test the port/cable with another device to isolate the fault
prevention: Keep network adapter drivers updated
Avoid disabling network adapters unless necessary
Regularly inspect physical connections on frequently moved equipment

description: The Ethernet connection shows as connected with a valid IP address, but there is still no internet access.
symptoms: Ethernet status shows 'Connected' with no warning
Local network devices may be reachable
Websites and online services do not load
possible_causes: Router has no internet from the ISP (WAN down)
DNS server not resolving correctly
Incorrect gateway configuration
Firewall blocking internet traffic despite local connectivity
ISP outage
diagnostic_questions: Does the network icon show fully connected with no warning triangle?
Can you access other devices on the local network, like a shared printer or file server?
Can you ping the router's IP address successfully?
Does the router's WAN/internet light look normal?

commands.purpose: Confirm the computer has a valid local IP, gateway, and DNS
commands.expected_result: Valid private IP address with a correct gateway matching the router
commands.abnormal_result: Missing or incorrect gateway/DNS entries explain the lack of internet despite local connection

commands.purpose: Test connectivity to the router itself
commands.expected_result: Replies received, confirming the local network segment works
commands.abnormal_result: Timeout means even the local connection to the router has an issue

commands.purpose: Test connectivity beyond the local router to the wider internet
commands.expected_result: Replies received
commands.abnormal_result: Timeout while the gateway ping succeeds confirms the router itself has no internet (WAN down)

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping the router's gateway IP address to confirm the local connection is healthy
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Separates a local network problem from an internet (WAN) problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping a known public IP address like 8.8.8.8 to test beyond the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If the gateway responds but this fails, the problem is the router's internet connection, not the computer

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router's WAN/internet status light and admin page for a connected status
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether the router itself has lost its ISP connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the modem and router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves many temporary WAN connectivity issues

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check firewall settings on the computer if other devices on the same network do have internet
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A local firewall issue can block internet while allowing local network access

troubleshooting_steps.action: Contact the ISP if the router confirms no WAN connection after a restart
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Indicates an outage or line issue outside local control

possible_solutions: Restart modem and router to restore WAN connection
Check and correct DNS/gateway settings
Adjust firewall rules if only this device is affected
Contact ISP if WAN remains down after restart
prevention: Monitor router WAN status periodically
Keep modem and router firmware updated
Use a UPS to prevent power-related WAN drops

description: Windows shows the network as 'Unidentified Network' after connecting an Ethernet cable, often with limited or no internet access.
symptoms: Network name shows as 'Unidentified Network' in Windows
Network may be categorized as public even on a trusted network
Internet access may be limited or missing
possible_causes: Windows could not properly detect the network's identity or gateway
Router or switch not responding correctly to network discovery
IP configuration incomplete or incorrect
Faulty cable or port causing an unstable connection
diagnostic_questions: Does this happen every time you connect, or only occasionally?
Is this a new router, network, or cable setup?
Does ipconfig show a complete IP configuration including a gateway?
Have you tried a different cable or port?

commands.purpose: Check whether the adapter received a complete network configuration
commands.expected_result: Full configuration including IP, subnet, gateway, and DNS
commands.abnormal_result: Missing gateway or an APIPA address explains why Windows cannot identify the network

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run ipconfig /all to check if a complete network configuration, including a gateway, was received
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An incomplete configuration is the most common reason Windows cannot identify the network

troubleshooting_steps.action: Release and renew the IP address using ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Forces a fresh, hopefully complete, configuration request

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different cable and port to rule out a physical fault causing an unstable connection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An unstable link can prevent Windows from fully completing network detection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the computer and the router/switch
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears temporary state issues on both ends that may prevent proper identification

troubleshooting_steps.action: Manually set the network profile to Private if identification issues persist but connectivity is otherwise fine
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Allows normal local network features to work even if auto-identification is imperfect

possible_solutions: Release and renew the IP configuration
Try a different cable or port
Restart the computer and networking equipment
Manually set the network profile if needed
prevention: Ensure the router's DHCP service is functioning properly for all clients
Use quality cables to maintain a stable link
Keep network adapter drivers updated

description: The Ethernet network adapter has been disabled in Windows, so the wired connection cannot be used at all.
symptoms: Ethernet adapter shows greyed out in Network Connections
No Ethernet option appears active in network settings
Right-click menu shows an option to 'Enable' rather than 'Disable'
possible_causes: Adapter was accidentally disabled by a user
Group Policy or IT management disabled the adapter
A driver or Windows update disabled the adapter
Power management settings turned off the adapter
diagnostic_questions: Was the adapter intentionally disabled by anyone recently, such as during troubleshooting?
Is this a personal computer or a managed work/school computer?
Did this happen after a Windows update?
Are other adapters, like WiFi, working normally?

commands.purpose: List all network adapters and their enabled/disabled status
commands.expected_result: Ethernet adapter status shows 'Up' or at least 'Disconnected' rather than 'Disabled'
commands.abnormal_result: Status shows 'Disabled', confirming the adapter itself is turned off

commands.purpose: Enable a disabled Ethernet adapter from PowerShell
commands.expected_result: Adapter status changes to enabled/connected
commands.abnormal_result: Access denied error means PowerShell needs to be run as Administrator, or Group Policy is preventing the change

troubleshooting_steps.action: Open Network Connections (ncpa.cpl) and check if the Ethernet adapter icon appears greyed out
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms visually whether the adapter is disabled

troubleshooting_steps.action: Right-click the adapter and select 'Enable'
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is the direct and simplest fix if the adapter was just turned off

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the option is greyed out or reverts back to disabled, check with IT if this is a managed/work computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Group Policy on managed computers can intentionally keep certain adapters disabled

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check adapter power management settings under Device Manager to ensure 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' is unchecked
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Aggressive power saving can effectively disable the adapter under certain conditions

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the computer after enabling the adapter
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Ensures the change takes full effect

possible_solutions: Enable the adapter through Network Connections or Device Manager
Check and adjust power management settings for the adapter
Check with IT/administrator if Group Policy is disabling the adapter on a managed device
prevention: Avoid disabling network adapters unless necessary for troubleshooting
Document any intentional Group Policy restrictions for managed devices
Regularly review power management settings after Windows updates

description: The Ethernet adapter does not appear at all in Network Connections or Device Manager, as if the hardware does not exist.
symptoms: No Ethernet adapter listed in Network Connections
Device Manager does not show the Ethernet controller, or shows it as unknown
Wired connection cannot be configured or used at all
possible_causes: Network adapter driver not installed
Motherboard's onboard network hardware failure
Adapter disabled at the BIOS/UEFI level
Recent Windows update removed or corrupted the driver
Physical hardware fault, especially on desktop motherboards
diagnostic_questions: Is this a laptop or desktop, and is the Ethernet port built-in or a separate USB adapter?
Did this start after a Windows update, reinstall, or hardware change?
Have you checked Device Manager under 'Other devices' or 'Network adapters' for anything with a warning icon?
Have you checked the BIOS/UEFI settings to confirm onboard LAN is enabled?

commands.purpose: List all network-related devices Windows can detect, including ones without working drivers
commands.expected_result: Ethernet controller listed with status 'OK'
commands.abnormal_result: Ethernet controller missing entirely, or listed with an error/unknown status

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Device Manager under 'Network adapters' and also 'Other devices' for anything unrecognized
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A missing driver often shows the hardware as an unknown device rather than disappearing completely

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the computer's BIOS/UEFI settings to confirm onboard LAN/Ethernet is enabled
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some systems allow disabling onboard network hardware at the firmware level

troubleshooting_steps.action: Download and install the correct network adapter driver directly from the motherboard or laptop manufacturer's website
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Ensures Windows has the correct driver to recognize and use the hardware

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a USB-to-Ethernet adapter as a test if the built-in port is suspected to have failed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Helps determine if this is a hardware failure versus a software/driver issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider professional repair or a USB Ethernet adapter as a permanent workaround if onboard hardware has failed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A confirmed hardware failure on a motherboard's LAN chip typically cannot be fixed through software

possible_solutions: Install the correct network adapter driver from the manufacturer
Enable onboard LAN in BIOS/UEFI if disabled
Use a USB-to-Ethernet adapter as a workaround for failed hardware
Seek professional repair for confirmed hardware failure
prevention: Keep chipset and network drivers updated
Avoid unnecessary BIOS/UEFI changes to hardware settings
Keep a USB Ethernet adapter on hand as a backup for critical systems

description: The Ethernet adapter hardware is recognized by Windows, but no driver is installed, so it cannot be used to connect to a network.
symptoms: Device Manager shows the Ethernet controller with a yellow warning icon
Error message: 'The drivers for this device are not installed'
No Ethernet option available in network settings
possible_causes: Fresh Windows installation without network drivers
Driver was uninstalled or corrupted
Windows Update did not provide a compatible driver automatically
diagnostic_questions: Was this a fresh Windows installation or reset?
Do you have another way to get online, such as WiFi or a USB drive with the driver on another computer?
What is the exact motherboard or laptop model, to find the correct driver?

commands.purpose: Confirm the adapter is detected as hardware even without a working driver
commands.expected_result: Device listed with a status indicating a driver problem
commands.abnormal_result: Status explicitly shows 'Error' or 'Unknown', confirming the driver is missing or not functioning

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Device Manager for the Ethernet controller under 'Other devices' with a warning icon
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms the hardware is detected but lacks a working driver

troubleshooting_steps.action: Use another internet-connected device to download the correct driver from the motherboard or laptop manufacturer's website
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Without a network driver, this computer cannot download it itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Transfer the driver installer to the affected computer using a USB drive
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides the only way to install the driver without existing network access

troubleshooting_steps.action: Install the driver and restart the computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Completes the installation and applies the changes

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the Ethernet adapter now appears normally in Device Manager and Network Connections
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Verifies the driver installed correctly and the adapter is usable

possible_solutions: Download and install the correct driver from the manufacturer using another device, then transfer via USB
Use Windows Update to search for a compatible driver if any other network connection is available
Run the manufacturer's full driver support package if available
prevention: Keep a copy of network drivers saved externally for quick recovery after OS reinstalls
Check manufacturer support pages for driver downloads before reinstalling Windows
Use a USB WiFi adapter as an alternative internet source during recovery

description: The Ethernet driver is installed but not functioning correctly, causing connection failures, errors, or inconsistent behavior.
symptoms: Adapter shows in Device Manager but with a warning icon or error code
Connection frequently drops or fails to establish
Error codes like 'Code 10' or 'Code 31' appear in Device Manager
possible_causes: Driver files corrupted due to an incomplete update or crash
Conflict with another recently installed driver or software
Malware damage to system driver files
Incompatible driver version for the current Windows build
diagnostic_questions: What exact error code, if any, shows in Device Manager for this adapter?
Did this start after a Windows update or new software installation?
Have you tried updating or reinstalling the driver already?
Does the problem happen consistently or only intermittently?

commands.purpose: List network devices currently reporting an error status
commands.expected_result: No devices returned (no errors)
commands.abnormal_result: Ethernet adapter listed, confirming a driver-level error

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the exact error code shown in Device Manager for the adapter
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Specific error codes point to specific documented causes and fixes from Microsoft

troubleshooting_steps.action: Uninstall the driver completely through Device Manager, including deleting the driver software if prompted
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Ensures no corrupted files remain before reinstalling

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the computer to let Windows attempt to reinstall a basic driver automatically
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Windows often reinstalls a default driver on restart after removal

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the basic driver does not resolve it, manually install the latest driver from the manufacturer's website
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides a clean, up-to-date, and compatible driver

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run a malware scan if driver corruption happens repeatedly without a clear cause
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out malicious software damaging system files

possible_solutions: Uninstall and reinstall the Ethernet driver completely
Install the latest driver from the manufacturer's website
Run System File Checker (sfc /scannow) to repair corrupted system files
Run a malware scan if corruption recurs
prevention: Keep drivers updated through official manufacturer channels
Avoid interrupting driver installations or Windows updates
Run regular malware scans to protect system files

description: The network connection works but is limited to 100 Mbps instead of the expected higher gigabit speed, even though the hardware supports it.
symptoms: Network adapter properties show link speed as 100 Mbps instead of 1.0 Gbps
File transfers between local devices are slower than expected
Internet speed itself may be fine if the plan is under 100 Mbps, but local transfers suffer
possible_causes: Damaged or low-category cable (Cat5 instead of Cat5e/Cat6)
Faulty port on the switch, router, or computer negotiating at a lower speed
Auto-negotiation failure between devices
Outdated network driver limiting speed
diagnostic_questions: What category of Ethernet cable is being used, if known (Cat5, Cat5e, Cat6)?
Are both the computer's network adapter and the switch/router port gigabit-capable?
Has this always been 100 Mbps, or did it recently drop from a higher speed?
Have you tried a different cable or port?

commands.purpose: Check the currently negotiated link speed of the network adapter
commands.expected_result: Shows 1 Gbps or higher on capable hardware
commands.abnormal_result: Shows 100 Mbps despite gigabit-capable hardware, confirming a negotiation or cable issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the network adapter's reported link speed using Get-NetAdapter or adapter properties
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms the actual negotiated speed versus the expected capability

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the Ethernet cable is at least Cat5e, ideally Cat6, since older Cat5 cables cannot support gigabit speeds reliably
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Cable category is a very common and simple cause of this limitation

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different cable and a different port on the switch or router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a damaged cable or a switch/router port stuck at a lower negotiated speed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the adapter's advanced settings for a manually forced speed setting instead of auto-negotiation
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A manually forced 100 Mbps setting will override the hardware's true capability

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the network adapter driver to the latest version
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Driver bugs can sometimes cause incorrect speed negotiation

possible_solutions: Replace the cable with a Cat5e or Cat6 cable
Try a different switch/router port
Set the adapter speed/duplex setting to 'Auto Negotiation' instead of a fixed value
Update the network adapter driver
prevention: Use Cat5e or better cabling for all new installations
Label cable categories during installation for future reference
Keep adapter settings on auto-negotiation unless there is a specific reason to force a setting

description: The small link/activity light next to the Ethernet port is completely off or stays solid without ever blinking, suggesting no active data connection.
symptoms: Link light is off or does not blink during normal use
No network connectivity through the wired port
May be accompanied by a 'cable unplugged' message
possible_causes: Cable not properly connected or damaged
Faulty port on the computer, switch, or router
Adapter disabled or driver not functioning
No power to the switch or router the cable connects to
diagnostic_questions: Is the light completely off, or on but never blinking during activity?
Have you confirmed both ends of the cable are firmly connected?
Is the switch or router the cable connects to powered on?
Have you tested this exact cable and port combination with another device?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the switch or router on the other end of the cable is powered on
troubleshooting_steps.reason: No power on the far end means there will never be a link, regardless of the local port

troubleshooting_steps.action: Firmly reseat the cable at both ends
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A loose connection can prevent the link light from activating even if it looks plugged in

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different, known-working cable
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a damaged cable preventing link establishment

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different port on the switch or router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Isolates whether the specific port on the networking equipment has failed

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Device Manager to confirm the network adapter is enabled and has no driver errors
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A disabled or malfunctioning adapter will not establish a link even with a good cable

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the cable and port with a different computer if the problem persists
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether the issue is with this specific computer's port/adapter or the networking equipment

possible_solutions: Reseat or replace the cable
Use a different port on the switch/router
Confirm power to the switch/router
Enable or repair the network adapter on the computer
prevention: Regularly inspect physical connections on critical systems
Label and test spare cables periodically
Keep networking equipment powered by a UPS to avoid unexpected outages

description: Neither the Ethernet nor WiFi adapter (or a specific one) is detected by the operating system at all, leaving no way to configure networking.
symptoms: No network adapters appear in Network Connections
Device Manager shows no network adapters, or an unknown device
No way to connect to any network, wired or wireless, depending on which adapter is affected
possible_causes: Driver not installed for the adapter
Hardware failure of the network adapter
Adapter disabled in BIOS/UEFI
Physical damage to the adapter, especially for add-in cards or USB adapters
diagnostic_questions: Is this affecting the Ethernet adapter, WiFi adapter, or both?
Is this a built-in adapter or an external USB/PCIe adapter?
Did this happen after a Windows reinstall, update, or hardware change?
Have you checked BIOS/UEFI to confirm the adapter is enabled?

commands.purpose: List all network devices Windows can detect, even with driver problems
commands.expected_result: All expected adapters listed with 'OK' status
commands.abnormal_result: Adapters missing entirely, indicating either a disabled, failed, or undetected hardware component

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check Device Manager thoroughly, including 'Other devices' and hidden devices, for any trace of the adapter
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An adapter without a driver often appears as an unknown device rather than disappearing completely

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check BIOS/UEFI settings to confirm the relevant onboard adapter is enabled
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some systems allow network adapters to be disabled at the firmware level

troubleshooting_steps.action: For external adapters, try a different USB port or PCIe slot
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a faulty port or slot rather than the adapter itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Install the correct driver from the manufacturer using another computer with internet access if needed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides the correct driver when Windows cannot detect or auto-install one

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider the adapter hardware failed if it still is not detected after driver installation and BIOS checks, and plan for replacement
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms a hardware fault that software troubleshooting cannot resolve

possible_solutions: Enable the adapter in BIOS/UEFI if disabled
Install the correct manufacturer driver
Try a different port/slot for external adapters
Replace the adapter if hardware failure is confirmed
prevention: Keep BIOS/UEFI settings documented after any changes
Handle add-in cards and USB adapters carefully to avoid physical damage
Keep driver installers backed up externally

description: The desired WiFi network name (SSID) does not appear in the list of available networks, even though the router is on and other devices can see it.
symptoms: Target WiFi network missing from the available networks list
Other WiFi networks nearby are visible
Other devices can see and connect to the same network
possible_causes: Router broadcasting on a WiFi band or channel the device does not support
Network is hidden (SSID broadcast disabled)
WiFi adapter disabled or malfunctioning on the affected device
Device is out of range or blocked by interference
Router's WiFi radio has crashed or is disabled
diagnostic_questions: Can other devices see and connect to this exact network name?
Is your device far from the router, or are there many walls/obstructions?
Do you know if the router uses 5GHz, 2.4GHz, or both, and does your device support that band?
Is the network hidden, or should it normally be visible?

commands.purpose: List all WiFi networks the adapter can currently detect
commands.expected_result: Target network appears in the list with a signal strength value
commands.abnormal_result: Target network missing from the list even though other networks are shown, confirming a detection or compatibility issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm on another device that the network is broadcasting normally and visible
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Establishes whether the problem is with the router or just this one device

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the router is using a WiFi band, like 5GHz, that this specific device may not support
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Older devices sometimes cannot see or connect to 5GHz-only networks

troubleshooting_steps.action: Move closer to the router and retry scanning for networks
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out range or interference as the cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Toggle WiFi off and on, or restart the WiFi adapter through Device Manager
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves a stuck or crashed WiFi radio state on the device

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check router settings to confirm SSID broadcast is enabled if the network should not be hidden
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A hidden network requires manual entry rather than appearing in the scan list

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router if its WiFi radio may have crashed while other functions still work
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A router-side radio crash will make the network invisible to all devices

possible_solutions: Restart the WiFi adapter or toggle WiFi off and on
Move closer to the router to rule out range issues
Enable SSID broadcast on the router if unintentionally hidden
Restart the router to reset its WiFi radio
Manually add the network if it is intentionally hidden
prevention: Choose WiFi bands and channels supported by all household/office devices
Keep router firmware updated
Avoid placing the router in an isolated or obstructed location

description: The WiFi network is visible in the list, but the device fails to connect, either hanging on 'Connecting' or returning an error.
symptoms: Connection attempt hangs on 'Connecting...' indefinitely
Error message appears such as 'Can't connect to this network'
Other devices connect to the same network without issue
possible_causes: Incorrect WiFi password entered
Router's maximum connected device limit reached
MAC address filtering blocking this specific device
Corrupted saved network profile on this device
WiFi driver issue
diagnostic_questions: Are you certain the WiFi password being entered is correct and current?
How many devices are currently connected to this network?
Does this device connect fine to other WiFi networks?
Have you tried forgetting this network and reconnecting from scratch?

commands.command: netsh wlan show profile name="<network_name>" key=clear
commands.purpose: View the saved WiFi password Windows has stored for this network profile
commands.expected_result: Shows the correct, current WiFi password
commands.abnormal_result: Shows an outdated or incorrect password, explaining the connection failure

troubleshooting_steps.action: Double-check the WiFi password being used matches the current router password exactly, watching for case sensitivity
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An incorrect password is by far the most common cause of connection failure

troubleshooting_steps.action: Forget the network on the device and reconnect from scratch, entering the password fresh
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears any corrupted or outdated saved profile causing silent failures

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router admin page for the number of currently connected devices versus its maximum supported limit
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some routers silently refuse new connections once a device limit is reached

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router's MAC address filtering settings, if enabled, to confirm this device is allowed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: MAC filtering can block a legitimate device that was never added to the allow list

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart both the router and the device's WiFi adapter
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears temporary state issues on both ends that can prevent a successful handshake

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the WiFi adapter driver if the device fails to connect to this network specifically but not others
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Driver bugs can cause compatibility issues with specific router models or security settings

possible_solutions: Forget and reconnect to the network with the correct password
Check and adjust MAC address filtering on the router
Restart the router and the device's WiFi adapter
Update the WiFi driver
Reduce connected devices if the router's limit is reached
prevention: Keep WiFi passwords documented securely for authorized users
Regularly review MAC filtering lists if used
Choose router hardware rated for the expected number of connected devices

description: The device rejects the WiFi password as incorrect, even though the user believes they are entering the correct one.
symptoms: Error message specifically indicates an incorrect network security key or password
Connection fails immediately after entering the password
Other devices connect successfully with the same password
possible_causes: Password was mistyped, including case sensitivity errors
Router's WiFi password was recently changed
Saved/cached password on the device is outdated
Confusion between similar network names, such as 2.4GHz and 5GHz versions with different passwords
diagnostic_questions: Are you sure of the exact current WiFi password, including uppercase and lowercase letters?
Has the WiFi password been changed recently by anyone with router access?
Are there multiple networks with similar names, like 'HomeWiFi' and 'HomeWiFi_5G', that might use different passwords?
Does this device have a previously saved profile for this network that might be outdated?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Carefully re-type the WiFi password, double-checking uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Simple typos are the most frequent cause of this exact error

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router's admin page or a label on the router itself for the correct current password
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms the actual current password rather than relying on memory

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm you are connecting to the correct network name if multiple similar SSIDs exist
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Prevents accidentally trying a 5GHz password on the 2.4GHz network or vice versa

troubleshooting_steps.action: Forget the saved network profile on the device and reconnect fresh with the correct password
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Removes any outdated cached password causing repeated rejection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Change the WiFi password on the router if it may have been changed unexpectedly by someone else, then reconnect all devices
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves confusion when the password was changed without the user's knowledge

possible_solutions: Re-enter the password carefully, checking case sensitivity
Confirm the correct password from the router directly
Forget and reconnect to the network with the correct password
Change the router's WiFi password if needed and update all devices
prevention: Use a password manager to store WiFi credentials accurately
Label the router with its current WiFi credentials in a secure location
Communicate password changes to all users of the network

description: The device connects partway to the WiFi network but then shows an 'Authentication failed' or similar error, disconnecting shortly after.
symptoms: Device briefly shows connected, then disconnects with an authentication error
Repeated connection attempts fail the same way
Other devices may or may not be affected
possible_causes: Incorrect or outdated WiFi password/security key
Mismatched security protocol between device and router, such as WPA2 vs WPA3
Router's authentication server or radio malfunctioning
Corrupted network profile on the device
MAC address filtering rejecting the device after initial handshake
diagnostic_questions: Does this happen with a fresh password entry, or does it happen even though the password is correct?
What WiFi security type does the router use, such as WPA2-Personal or WPA3?
Is this a new or recently updated device that may not support the router's security protocol?
Does restarting the router or the device change anything?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the exact WiFi password is correct by checking it directly from the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Even with authentication-specific errors, an incorrect password remains a common root cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check what WiFi security protocol the router is using and whether the device supports it
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Older devices may not support newer protocols like WPA3, causing authentication failures

troubleshooting_steps.action: Forget the network profile on the device and reconnect from scratch
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears potentially corrupted authentication data cached from a previous connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router to reset its wireless authentication process
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves temporary glitches in the router's handling of client authentication

troubleshooting_steps.action: Temporarily switch the router's security mode to a more widely compatible setting like WPA2-Personal (AES) to test compatibility
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether a security protocol mismatch is the root cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update the WiFi adapter driver on the device if the issue is isolated to one device
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Driver-level bugs can cause authentication handshakes to fail with certain routers

possible_solutions: Forget and reconnect using the correct password
Switch router security mode to a more compatible setting if needed
Restart the router
